author: claude fresh independent technology SME recheck critic (jdbc-data-access 2026-11-09)

findings.claim: The new URL builder tests the jdbc: prefix case-insensitively (/^jdbc:/i, line 488) but the subprotocol case-sensitively, so input 'JDBC:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop' is told the subprotocol 'postgresql' must be spelled in full and in lower case, although the learner's subprotocol is already correct. pgJDBC rejects the URL because the whole prefix 'jdbc:postgresql:' is matched case-sensitively, so the feedback names the wrong part. All other variants run in node give accurate messages: the canonical URL and surrounding whitespace pass; missing jdbc:, jdbc:postgres:, missing //, wrong host/port/database, empty port and query parameters are refused with accurate, task-scoped messages, and the 'Without a port pgJDBC would assume 5432' message matches the documented default.

evidence.section: Connecting to the Database: URL forms (all lower-case jdbc:postgresql:)

findings.recommendation: Make the first check case-sensitive (/^jdbc:/) and say 'starts with jdbc: in lower case', or add a case-specific message when /^jdbc:postgresql:/i matches but the exact prefix does not.
